acceptance_criteria: check_known_capabilities([core, mail], req_with_unknown) returns Err(unknownCapability); check_known_capabilities([core, mail], req_with_known) returns Ok(()); parse_request doc updated with caller-responsibility note
close_reason: check_known_capabilities() added to jmap-server/parse.rs, re-exported from lib.rs, 3 unit tests pass
description: parse_request accepts unknown capability URIs in using (intentionally, as the test parse_request_unknown_capability_accepted documents). But rfc-clarifications.md Q3 rules that unknown capability URIs in using MUST produce an HTTP-level 4xx error — not a method-level error, and not silent acceptance. Currently consumers get no help from the library for this check.
design:
Add a helper function to jmap-server: pub fn check_known_capabilities(req: &JmapRequest, known: &[&str]) -> Result<(), JmapError> that returns unknownCapability JmapError if any URI in req.using is not in the known set. Consumers call this immediately after parse_request and map the error to HTTP 400. Document clearly in parse_request doc comment that capability URI validation is the caller's responsibility and point to check_known_capabilities.

Separately: update parse_request doc comment to reference Q3 ruling: unknown capability in using → caller must return HTTP 4xx (not the library, since the library doesn't know which capabilities the server supports).

Ref: rfc-clarifications.md Q1 (notRequest MUST be 400), Q3 (unknown capability MUST be HTTP 4xx); jmap-test-suite error-unknown-capability test.
title: jmap-server: document+expose unknown-capability validation as caller responsibility
